# Your Rails models. An admin interface.

AdminSuite turns resource definitions into searchable tables, forms, record
pages, and dashboards. Mount it in your Rails application and keep authentication,
authorization, and business logic under your control.
{: .fs-6 .fw-300 }

[Get started]({{ '/installation/' | relative_url }}){: .btn .btn-primary .mr-2 }
[Explore the resource DSL]({{ '/resources/' | relative_url }}){: .btn }

## Install, mount, configure

```bash
bundle add admin_suite
bin/rails generate admin_suite:install
```

The generator mounts the engine at `/internal/admin`. Configure authentication
before opening it, then add your first resource.

```ruby
AdminSuite.configure do |config|
  config.auth_strategy = :host_user
  config.auth_options = { resolve: ->(controller) { controller.current_user } }
  config.authorize = ->(actor:, action:, resource:, record:, context:) { actor&.admin? }
end
```

Use your application's own user resolver and access policy. Read the
[authentication guide]({{ '/authentication/' | relative_url }}) for fail-closed behavior, HTTP Basic,
custom strategies, and record authorization.

## Give operators read access through MCP

The operator MCP endpoint exposes four read tools derived from the same resource
DSL: discover resources, list records, read a record, and aggregate a collection.
It requires an authenticated actor and an explicit authorization hook. No write
tools or embedded assistant are included.

[Configure Admin MCP]({{ '/mcp/' | relative_url }})

## Requirements and support

AdminSuite requires Ruby 3.2 or newer and Rails 8.x. Your selected Rails release
may impose a higher Ruby minimum. Use the gem's dependency resolution to select
a compatible combination.

See [Troubleshooting]({{ '/troubleshooting/' | relative_url }}), browse the
[configuration reference]({{ '/configuration/' | relative_url }}), or
[open an issue](https://github.com/techwright-lab/admin_suite/issues).
